senses.gloss: कत m. Strychnos Potatorum (cf. the next), L.
N. of a Ṛṣi, Pāṇ.
कान्त &c. See s.v.
कत—फल n. = the next.
कतक m. Strychnos Potatorum or the clearing nut plant (its seeds rubbed upon the inside of water-jars precipitate the earthy particles in the water, W.), Mn. vi, 67; Suśr.
N. of a commentator on the Rāmāyaṇa.
कतम॑ (अस्), (आ), (अत्), mfn. (superlative of 2. क; declined as a pronom., Gram. 236), who or which of many? (e.g. कतमेन पथा यातास् ते, by which road have they gone?)
it is often a mere strengthened substitute for क, the superlative affix imparting emphasis
hence it may occasionally be used for ‘who or which of two?’ (e.g. तयोः कतमस्मै, to which of these two?)
it may optionally be compounded with the word to which it refers (e.g. कतमः कठः, or कतम-कठः, which Kaṭha out of many?)

when followed by च and preceded यतम an indefinite expression is formed equivalent to ‘any whosoever’, ‘any whatsoever’, &c. (e.g. यतमद् एव कतमच् च विद्यात् he may know anything whatsoever). In negative sentences कतम with चन or कतम with अपि = not even one, none at all (e.g. न कतमच्चनाहः, not even on a single day, on no day at all)
in addition to the above uses कतम is said to mean ‘best’, ‘excessively good-looking’ (cf. 3. क), RV. &c.
कतमोरग m. N. of a man.

कतर॑ (अस्, आ, अत्), mfn. (comparative of 2. क; declined as a pronom., Gram. 236), who or which of two? whether of two? Analogously to कतम above कतर may occasionally be used to express ‘who or which of many?’ (e.g. कतरस्यां दिशि, in which quarter?), and may optionally be compounded with the word to which it refers (e.g. कतरः कठः or कतर-कठः)
in negative sentences कतर with चन = neither of the two (e.g. न कतरश्-चन जिग्ये), neither of the two was conquered, RV. &c.;
कतर [cf. Zd. katāra; Gk. πότερος, κότερος; Goth. hvathar; Eng. whether; Lat. uter; Old Germ. huedar; Slav. kotoryi.]

कातर mf(आ)n. (etym. doubtful, perhaps from कतर, ‘uncertain as to which of the two’, BRD.), cowardly, faint-hearted, timid, despairing, discouraged, disheartened, confused, agitated, perplexed, embarrassed, shrinking, frightened, afraid of (loc. or inf. or in comp.), R.; Mṛcch.; Ragh.; Megh.; Śak.; Pañcat.; Hit.
कातर m. a kind of large fish (Cyprinus Catla, कातल), L.
N. of a man (see कातरायण)
कातर n. (in स-कातर) ‘timidity, despair, agitation’.
कतर—तस् ind. on which of the two sides? ŚBr. vi.
कतरथा ind. in which of two manners or ways?, ṢaḍvBr.

1. क॑ति (fr. 2. क declined in pl. only, Gram. 227 a; all the cases except the nom. voc. and acc. taking terminations, whereas the correlative इति has become fixed as an indeclinable adverb), how many? quot? several (e.g. कति देवाः, how many gods? कति व्यापादयति कति वा ताडयति, some he kills and some he strikes). In the sense of ‘several’, ‘some’, कति is generally followed by चिद् or अपि (e.g. कतिचिद् अहानि, for several or some days)
it may be used as an adverb with चिद् in the sense of ‘oftentimes’, ‘much’, ‘in many ways’ (e.g. कतिचित् स्तुतः, much or often praised), RV. &c.;
कति [cf. Zd. caiti; Gk. πόστος; Lat. quot; cf. Sk. तति and Lat. tot.]
2. कति (for 1. See above) m. N. of a sage (son of Viśvā-mitra and ancestor of Kātyāyana), Hariv.
काति mfn. (fr. √ 3. का), ‘wishing, desiring’ (only in comp. See ऋण॑-काति and का॑म-काति cf. ऋण-चि॑त्)
काति m. pl. N. of a school.
कति—कृत्वस् ind. how many times? Vop. (cf. कति, कृ॑त्वस्, ŚBr. xii, 3, 2, 7.)
कति—भेद mfn. of how many divisions or kinds? Car.
कति—विध mfn. of how many kinds?
कति—शस् ind. how many at a time? Kum.
कति—संख्य mfn. how many in number? Pañcat.
कति—हायन mfn. how many years old? Bālar.
1. कतिक mfn. (for 2. See below) how many? Car.
bought for how much? Pat.
2. कतिक (for 1. See above) n. N. of a town, Rājat.
कतितिथ mfn. with following चिद् or च, the so-maniest, Bālar.
कतिथ॑ mfn. the how-maniest? Pāṇ. v, 2, 51
with चिद्, the so-maniest, RV. x, 61, 18 (= कतिपयानां पूरणः, Sāy.)
to such and such a point
कतिथ [cf. Gk. πόστος; Lat. quotus.]
कतिधा॑ ind. how many times? how often? in how many places? in how many parts? RV. &c.
with चिद्, everywhere, RV. i, 31, 2.
कतिपय॑ mf(ई, आ [only BhP. ix, 18, 39])n. (m. pl. ए and आस्) several, some
a certain number, so many (e.g. कतिपयेनाहर्-गणेन, after some days; also कतिपयैर् अहोभिः, कतिपयाहस्य, &c.), ŚBr. &c.
कतिपय॑ (अम्), n. a little, some (at the end of Tatpuruṣa compounds, e.g. उदश्वित्-कतिपयम्, a little Udaśvit), Pāṇ. ii, 1, 65
कतिप˚येन (एन), ind. with some exertion, with difficulty, narrowly, Pāṇ. ii, 3, 33.
कतिप˚यात् (आत्), ind. with some exertion, with difficulty, narrowly, Pāṇ. ii, 3, 33.
कतिपयथ mfn. somewhat advanced, somaniest, Kāṭh.; Pāṇ. v, 2, 51.
कतमाल m. fire, L.
(incorrect for खतमाल, BRD.; cf. कचमाल, करमाल.)
कतीमुष m. N. of an Agrahāra, Rājat.
कत्ता-शब्द m. the rattling sound of dice, Mṛcch.
कत्-तृण &c. See 2. कद्.
का-तृण n. ‘bad grass’, a particular kind of grass (Rohiṣa-tṛṇa), L. (cf. कत्तृण.)
कत्थक m. N. of a man.
कात्थक m. ‘descendant of Katthaka’, N. of a commentator, Nir.
कत्थन mfn. boasting, praising, MBh.; R.
कत्थन n. the act of boasting, MBh.; R.; Suśr.
कत्थना f. id. Comm. on Bhaṭṭ.
कत्थित n. boasting, MBh. i, 5995.
कत्थितव्य mfn. to be boasted, Car.
कत्-पय॑ mfn. (fr. 2. कद् and पय fr. √ प्यै, BRD.), swelling, rising, RV. v, 32, 6
(= सुख-पयस्, Nir. vi, 3 ; and accordingly = सुख-करं पयो यस्य, Sāy.)
कत्र् cl. 10. P. कत्रयति, to loosen, slacken, remove, Dhātup. xxxv, 60 (cf. कर्त्, कर्त्र्.)
कत्सवर m. the shoulder, shoulder-blade, L.
कत् (in comp. for 2. कद् above).
कात् ind. a prefix implying contempt (cf. 2. कद्), only in comp. with
कत्—तृन n. a fragrant grass, Suśr.
Pistia Stratiotes, L.
कत्—तोय n. an intoxicating drink, wine or vinous spirit, L.
कत्—त्रि mfn. pl. three inferior (persons or articles &c.) Vārtt. on Pāṇ. vi, 3, 101.
कत्—त्र्य्-आदि m. N. of a gaṇa, Pāṇ. iv, 2, 95 (cf. कात्त्रेयक.)
कात्—√ कृ ‘to insult, dishonour’ p.p. कात्-कृत mfn. insulted, dishonoured, BhP. vi, 7, 11.
कात्-√ कृ See कात्.
का-तन्त्र n. N. of a grammar, also called कलापक, or ˚प-सूत्र or कौमारव्याकरण (composed by Śrī-śarvavarman ‘after the Sūtra composed by Bhagavat-Kumāra, and at his command’)
का-तन्त्र m. pl. the followers of the Kātantra grammar.

का-तन्त्र—कौमुदी f. N. of a comm. on the above by Go-vardhana. Other similar works are: -गण-धातु, -चतुष्टय-प्रदीप, -चन्द्रिका, -धातु-घोषा, -पञ्जिका, -परिशिष्ट, -परिशिष्ट-प्रबोध, -लघु-वृत्ति, -विभ्रमसूत्र, -विस्तर or -विस्तार, -वृत्ति, -वृत्ति-टीका, -वृत्ति-पञ्जिका, -शब्द-माला, -षट्-कारक, and कातन्त्रोणादि-वृत्ति.
कातर—ता, f. or कातर—त्व, n. cowardice, timidity, agitation, Śak.; Megh.; Pañcat.
कातर—ता, f. or कातर—त्व, n. cowardice, timidity, agitation, Śak.; Megh.; Pañcat.
कातराक्षी f. a woman with timid eyes, Kāvyād. ii, 156.
कातरायण m. a descendant of Kātara g. नडादि.
कातर्य n. cowardice, timidity, dejection, agitation, fear, MBh.; R.; Ragh.
कातल m. a kind of large fish (Cyprinus Catla cf. कातर), L.
N. of a man g. नडादि.
कातलायन m. a descendant of Kātala g. नडादि (cf. कातरायण.)
कातीय mfn. (fr. कात्य), composed by Kātya.
कातीय—कल्प-सूत्र n. N. of wk.
कातीय—गृह्य-सूत्र n. N. of wk. by Pāraskara (belonging to the White Yajur-veda).
कातीय—सूत्र n. N. of wk.
का-तीर n. a bad shore, Pāṇ. vi, 1, 155, Kāś.
का॑तु m. = कूप, Naigh. iii, 23 (cf. काट॑.)
कात्त्रेयक mfn. (fr. 2. क॑द् + त्रि), produced from or pertaining to any combination of three inferior articles, Pāṇ. iv, 2, 95.
कात्य m. = कात्यायन, g. गर्गादि, Pāṇ. iv, 1, 105.

कात्यायन m. ‘descendant of Kati’ (see 2. कति), N. of the author of several treatises on ritual, grammar, &c., Hariv. 1461 and 1768; R. ii, 67, 2; VPrāt.; Yājñ. i, 4 (he is also author of the Vārttikas or critical annotations on the aphorisms of Pāṇini, of the Yajur-veda Prātiśākhya, and of the Śrauta-sūtras, and is identified with Vara-ruci, the author of the Prākṛta-prakāśa)
कात्यायन mf(ई)n. composed by Kātyāyana.
कात्यायनी॑ (ई॑), f. N. of one of the two wives of Yājñavalkya, ŚBr.
of a Pravrājikā, Kathās.
of Durgā, Hariv.; Lalit.; Prab.
a middle-aged widow dressed in red clothes, L.
कात्यायनी f. of ˚यन, q.v.
कात्यायन—तन्त्र n. N. of wk.
कात्यायन—माहात्म्य n. N. of wk.
कात्यायन—सूत्र n. the Śrauta-sūtras of Kātyāyana
कात्यायन—सूत्र—पद्धति f. a commentary on the same by Yājñika-deva
कात्यायन—सूत्र—भाष्य n. a commentary on the same by Karka.
कात्यायनेश्वर n. N. of a Liṅga, SkandaP.
कात्यायनिका f. a widow in middle age, L.
कात्यायनी—कल्प m. N. of a Kalpa.
कात्यायनी—पुत्र m. N. of a teacher, BṛĀrUp. vi, 5, 1.
कात्यायनीय m. pl. the school of Kātyāyana
कात्यायनीय n. N. of several works
कात्यायनीय mfn. composed by Kātyāyana (e.g. -शास्त्र, the law-book composed by Kātyāyana)
कात्यायनीय m. a pupil of Kātyāyana, W.
